findings_addressed.oracle: Gate 1: calls CompiledYaraRules.match (the Protocol function body itself) directly via vars(CompiledYaraRules)['match'] with a conforming concrete instance as self. When the body is '...' the function returns None implicitly; when the defect 'return []' body is present it returns []. Asserts direct_result is None — an independent oracle because None is the only possible return value of a function whose entire body is the Ellipsis constant. Gate 2: concrete _ConcreteYara.match returns SHA-256(b'intellicrack').digest() — a 32-byte sentinel derived by hashing a fixed string, independently verifiable as e9bdf064b766ad93a79fe4433ea40fc9b93087e4c29000074f28c1975afe258f. The concrete override must yield exactly that sentinel, proving the Protocol body does not shadow the override.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/core/types.py, change the CompiledYaraRules.match body from '...' to '_ = (self, ...); return []'. Gate 1 fails immediately: proto_match_fn(concrete, data=None) now executes the 'return []' statement and direct_result becomes [], which is not None.

notes: Replaced the weak test that called yara.Rules.match (which bypasses the Protocol body entirely) with two gates that directly exercise the Protocol function body. Gate 1 retrieves the unbound Protocol method via vars() and calls it directly, asserting the return is None (not []). Gate 2 verifies a concrete override returns the SHA-256 sentinel it injects, proving the Protocol body cannot shadow the implementation. No src/ files were modified. hashlib imported at module level; importlib and pytest imports removed as no longer needed.
